sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
sections.docs:
<docs>
Pi documentation (read only when the user asks about pi itself, its SDK, extensions, themes, skills, or TUI):
- Main documentation: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/README.md
- Additional docs: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs
- Examples: <vol>/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/examples (extensions, custom tools, SDK)
- When reading pi docs or examples, resolve docs/... under Additional docs and examples/... under Examples, not the current working directory
- When asked about: extensions (docs/extensions.md, examples/extensions/), themes (docs/themes.md), skills (docs/skills.md), prompt templates (docs/prompt-templates.md), TUI components (docs/tui.md), keybindings (docs/keybindings.md), SDK integrations (docs/sdk.md), custom providers (docs/custom-provider.md), adding models (docs/models.md), pi packages (docs/packages.md), environment variables (docs/environment-variables.md), MCP servers (docs/mcp.md), codemode scripts and non-LLM models such as classifiers and image models (docs/codemode.md)
- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)
</docs>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Create an SVG logo for a generative AI company using organic shapes and neutral tones

Deliver the result as image and/or video files, working in the current directory.
- Save the finished files in ./output/. Only what is in ./output/ is published as the result, so
  ./output/ holds those finished image/video files and nothing else.
- Formats: images as .png, .jpg, .webp, .gif or .svg; videos as .mp4 or .webm. At most 8 files,
  each under 2 MB; videos at most 10 seconds.
- Tools available on this machine: python3 3.15.0 (standard library only), node 26.12.0 (no npm packages), ffmpeg 9.0.2, ffprobe 9.0.2. Don't install packages or download anything.
- Keep the code you write to make the files in the working directory (its root, or a subdirectory
  like ./src/, but not in ./output/): it's published as the source. Delete intermediate files such
  as rendered frames when you're done.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you made.

content.thinking:
**Designing logo features**

I need to create a beautiful SVG logo with a wordmark that includes an invented organic icon called "loam," representing a neural sprout and a folded pebble. I want to keep it simple and avoid unnecessary overdesign. The main image will use warm, neutral colors like ivory and dark brown, focusing on connected lobes to suggest emergence. I’m considering names like "forma" or "loam" for the company. The logo design will incorporate a tagline and may need a refined organic symbol.

**Refining icon design**

I’m thinking of an icon design that features three rounded pebbles rotating around a central point, separated by curved negative spaces. The shape will resemble a triskelion, with droplet-shaped lobes pointing inward. Each organic lobe is defined by specific curves and should have no overlap when rotated. I'll also explore a design with a single closed blob featuring three apertures. Using neutral tones like taupe and varying the darkness of the lobes could create a strong, muted icon.

**Exploring SVG rendering options**

I need to implement manual SVG rendering and check if tools are available for that since there’s no native image raster support. I'm curious if ffmpeg supports SVG. Additionally, I might explore using qlmanage or sips on Mac for converting SVGs, though I don't think it's necessary. SVG seems excellent for my needs! I also want to create an artistic, custom wordmark for "loam" that smooths out the design using paths.

from pathlib import Path

OUT = Path('output')
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# A seed shape repeated around an open, three-way centre. Each Bézier
# contour is deliberately asymmetric: soft, living geometry rather than a gear.
seed = 'M 0,-14 C -18,-35 -59,-37 -71,-75 C -88,-124 -53,-163 -10,-163 C 34,-163 71,-129 61,-89 C 52,-51 19,-43 0,-14 Z'
colors = ['#544D42', '#938675', '#B9AA96']

def emblem(transform=''):
    return f'''<g transform="{transform}">
      <path d="{seed}" fill="{colors[0]}"/>
      <path d="{seed}" transform="rotate(120)" fill="{colors[1]}"/>
      <path d="{seed}" transform="rotate(240)" fill="{colors[2]}"/>
    </g>'''

# Lettering is drawn as vectors, not font-dependent text. Rounded joins and
# slightly open proportions echo the softness of the seed mark.
wordmark = '''<g fill="none" stroke="#393A32" stroke-width="19" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round">
    <path d="M 710,375 V 488 Q 710,515 735,515"/>
    <path d="M 837,469 C 837,441 822,422 795,422 C 768,422 753,441 753,469 C 753,497 768,516 795,516 C 822,516 837,497 837,469 Z"/>
    <path d="M 953,469 C 953,441 937,422 911,422 C 884,422 868,441 868,469 C 868,497 884,516 911,516 C 937,516 953,497 953,469 M 953,425 V 515"/>
    <path d="M 995,515 V 425 M 995,455 C 995,436 1009,422 1028,422 C 1048,422 1062,436 1062,456 V 515 M 1062,456 C 1062,436 1076,422 1096,422 C 1116,422 1130,436 1130,456 V 515"/>
  </g>'''

primary = f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1600" height="1000" viewBox="0 0 1600 1000" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">
  <title id="title">loam — generative AI</title>
  <desc id="desc">An organic three-seed emblem in warm earth tones, paired with a custom rounded lowercase loam wordmark on an ivory field.</desc>
  <rect width="1600" height="1000" fill="#F3F0E9"/>
  <g transform="translate(55 0)">
    {emblem('translate(475 483) scale(.88)')}
    {wordmark}
    <text x="711" y="578" fill="#817B6F" font-family="Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="500" letter-spacing="4.5">GENERATIVE AI</text>
  </g>
</svg>
'''
(OUT / 'loam-logo.svg').write_text(primary)

icon = f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="640" height="640" viewBox="0 0 640 640" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">
  <title id="title">loam — seed symbol</title>
  <desc id="desc">Three organic seed forms turn around an open centre, suggesting ideas growing into new possibilities.</desc>
  <rect width="640" height="640" rx="144" fill="#F3F0E9"/>
  {emblem('translate(320 337) scale(1.36)')}
</svg>
'''
(OUT / 'loam-symbol.svg').write_text(icon)

# A transparent, tightly cropped lockup for practical use on light surfaces.
transparent = f'''<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1000" height="360" viewBox="0 0 1000 360" role="img" aria-labelledby="title desc">
  <title id="title">loam</title>
  <desc id="desc">Transparent vector logo for loam, a generative AI company.</desc>
  <g transform="translate(-277 -300)">
    {emblem('translate(475 483) scale(.88)')}
    {wordmark}
  </g>
</svg>
'''
(OUT / 'loam-transparent.svg').write_text(transparent)
print('Created three SVG logo assets.')
